🇲🇽🌧️ <u>S&P: El Niño Puts 10 Mexican State Economies on the Line</u>

According to S&P National Ratings, cited by El Economista, more than 34% of state GDP in Baja California Sur, Durango, Jalisco, Morelos, Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Sinaloa, Tlaxcala, Veracruz and Yucatán comes from climate-sensitive tourism, farming and food industries. Nationally those sectors hold about 24% of local jobs, a share that averages 39% in Baja California Sur, Quintana Roo and Nayarit. The agency rates the national impact as moderate compared with other emerging markets. The squeeze lands on state budgets, which face slower growth and higher emergency spending at the same time.
banner: EL NIÑO: 10 STATES >34% OF GDP EXPOSED

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Right Still Celebrates the Conquest</u>

Since AMLO's December 2020 decree, Mexico has marked October 12 as the Day of the Pluricultural Nation instead of "Día de la Raza." The right hasn't let go. PAN Mexico City lawmaker América Rangel posts tributes to Hispanidad and to the fall of the Mexica empire. In May, Cuauhtémoc mayor Alessandra Rojo de la Vega received Madrid's Isabel Díaz Ayuso at her offices. On that same tour, at an event titled "Celebration of Evangelization and Mestizaje in Mexico," Ayuso declared: "Without Cortés, there would be no Mexico."

🇲🇽🏘️ <u>Sinaloa Gives Land to 60 Families Driven Out of Concordia by Violence</u>

Sixty families forced from their homes in Concordia received plots on Saturday in Mazatlán's CVIVE development. The land comes with drinking water, drainage and electricity already in place, so they can start building right away. Governor Graciela Domínguez put the investment at 5.5 million pesos. Another 30 plots in Mazatlán are still to be handed over, part of a program covering 53 hectares across the state.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>A Tax-Court Judge Reports 120 Forged Rulings and Gets Transferred for It</u>

Ricardo León Caraveo, a magistrate on the Federal Administrative Justice Court (TFJA) appointed by AMLO in January 2024, reported the court's governing board for more than 120 allegedly falsified rulings and sessions that never took place. He estimates the damage to the federal treasury at 1.4 trillion pesos. He was then moved from Jalisco to Tabasco, and on September 28 his security detail was pulled. "The Federal Administrative Justice Court is a farce," he says. "They are deceiving President Claudia Sheinbaum."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico's M&A Market Shrinks 25%, and Washington Is Still the Top Buyer</u>

According to TTR Data, reported by El Economista, Mexico closed 200 mergers and acquisitions through September worth $14.549 billion. That's 12% fewer deals than a year earlier, and 25% less money. Real estate (31 deals, capital up 48%) and industrial software (29) were the most active sectors. US buyers made 48 acquisitions in Mexico, more than any other country, with the UK a distant second at 10. Going the other way, Mexican companies put their money mostly into Spain (12 deals), then Brazil and the US (8 each).

🇲🇽🏥 <u>IMSS Walks Its Hospitals Floor by Floor and Finds 7,474 Needs</u>

After its workers demanded better conditions, Mexico's Social Security Institute sent teams through its hospitals floor by floor. So far, 166 of its 277 hospitals have been checked, 60%. Director Zoé Robledo reported 7,474 needs, 3,122 of them high priority. Medical equipment tops the list with 972 entries, from vital-sign monitors and stretchers to oximeters and infusion pumps. Next come 751 supply shortages (needles, catheters, syringes, glucose strips) and 522 maintenance problems, including air conditioning, water, oxygen outlets and beds. The next round covers subzone hospitals in Jalisco, western State of Mexico, Chihuahua and Sonora.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Guatemala's President Thanks Mexico, Land of Asylum, 72 Years After the CIA Coup</u>

On Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco's first visit to Guatemala, President Bernardo Arévalo unveiled a plaque at the old Mexican embassy. After the 1954 CIA-backed coup, that building sheltered more than 300 people persecuted by the new regime, including the overthrown president, Jacobo Árbenz. Arévalo, himself the son of an exile in Mexico, called the plaque an act of memory, gratitude and brotherhood. Velasco brought greetings from Sheinbaum and said asylum is one of the deepest convictions of Mexico's foreign policy. From Spain's Republicans in 1939 to Guatemala in 1954, the door stayed open.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Treason Charge for the Chihuahua Prosecutor Who Brought the CIA In</u>

Mexico's Attorney General Ernestina Godoy says César Jáuregui, Maru Campos's former state prosecutor, may have committed treason against the nation. The FGR found he organized the April raid on a drug lab in El Pinal, Chihuahua, with CIA agents taking part, kept federal authorities in the dark, and stayed in contact with US officials the whole time. Two of those agents died in a crash on the way back. After more than 100 investigative acts, a federal judge issued the warrant. In Godoy's words, it "violates the sovereignty and integrity of the nation, as it is expressly prohibited."

🇲🇽📉 <u>Mexico's Lowest Year-to-Date Inflation Since 2020, and Three States Where Prices Fell</u>

According to INEGI, consumer prices rose 2.12% from January to September 2026, the smallest increase for that period since 2020. Sonora (-0.58%), Baja California Sur (-0.43%) and Sinaloa (-0.20%) were the only states where prices fell. The main reason was electricity, through CFE's subsidized hot-season tariffs. Eggs were the second-biggest drag on prices. Jalisco had the highest rate in the country, at 3.88%.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN Rolls Out the Welcome Mat for Cabeza de Vaca in 2027</u>

PAN national leader Jorge Romero says it "would be an honor" for former Tamaulipas governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca to run for Congress in 2027. Romero insists there is no arrest warrant against him and calls the organized-crime and money-laundering investigations "political persecution." This is PAN's plan to win back Tamaulipas.
banner: PAN OPENS 2027 DOOR TO CABEZA DE VACA
